A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MV-MATH benchmark and experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices, including matching renumbered examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, a human performance study and error analyses on MV-MATH, with detailed results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the original model evaluations, human performance study and quantitative and qualitative error analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and annotation pipeline, prompting procedures and answer extraction approach are retained. No proposed algorithm, model architecture, training objective or inference component changes.

E1.justification: Both report the same 2,009-problem MV-MATH coverage: 11 subjects, three difficulty levels and multiple-choice, single-step and multi-step questions. Removing illustrative error cases does not establish removal of evaluated benchmark items.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–4 and 10–14, including the Deepseek-Chat text/caption controls, open-source and closed-source models, and human baseline. The new citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain the same prompting configurations, accuracy/SAR/QCR metrics, 200-item testmini human study with 50 students, and Appendix B generation settings. The corrected illustrative answer does not establish a changed evaluation protocol or rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix H removes v1 Figures 22, 24 and 29: a cube-net perception case, a cube-volume reasoning case and a cylinder-problem refusal. Seven examples covering all five error categories remain; the prompting, image-relevance/input analyses and aggregate 100-error analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point accuracy reporting without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figure 1 changes the displayed knight-move answer from 12 to 18, and three individual qualitative model outputs disappear with the removed error examples. Aggregate scores remain unchanged: Table 4 still reports Claude-3.5 at 33.9%, LLaVA-OneVision-Chat-72B at 26.2% and humans on testmini at 76.5%.

T1.justification: The coefficient-of-variation definition in Equation 1, SAR/QCR definitions and difficulty-labeling assumptions are unchanged. No theoretical proposition, proof or formal derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and claims about the model–human gap, cross-image reasoning challenges, image input ordering and inconsistent prompting benefits.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model generalization, image dependence, multi-step reasoning and LLaVA-OneVision training remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and the appendices. The reduced example set does not revise the error taxonomy or substantive limitations.

D1.justification: v5 adds a project-page link labeled 'The data and code' to the abstract; v1 has no corresponding access pointer. Appendix B retains the same hardware, model sources, prompts, temperature of 0.2 and 2,048-token generation limit.

R1.justification: v5 adds introductory citations to Wang et al.'s survey of multimodal pretrained models and Xu et al.'s work on automatic question tagging, references 42 and 46. The positioning against MathVerse-mv, CMM-Math and other benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 adds Xin Yang to the author list, reformats two author names, adds the access sentence and updates references and the Appendix H figure range. The section hierarchy and almost all substantive prose are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 has typography and spacing adjustments. Three appendix case figures are removed, retained cases are renumbered and the surviving refusal example occupies its own page. The other plots and table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 corrects Figure 1's knight-move answer from 12 to 18 and adds an explicit data/code access pointer, improving local accuracy and resource discoverability. Removing three error examples reduces illustrative breadth, but all five error categories and aggregate analyses remain. These are limited improvements rather than a substantive strengthening of the empirical evidence.
